accountant.title: Accountant
accountant.lede: Help individuals and businesses manage money, minimise tax, and make smart financial decisions.
dayInLife: Prepare financial statements, tax returns and budgets
Advise clients or management on financial decisions
Audit records for accuracy and compliance
Use accounting software to track and forecast cash flow

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: Mathematics (Standard or Advanced), Economics or Business Studies (recommended, not required)

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Bachelor of Commerce or Bachelor of Business (Accounting major) — 3 years

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Complete CA (Chartered Accountant) or CPA Australia professional program after your degree to become fully qualified

accountant.aiNote: Medium AI exposure — software already automates a lot of routine data entry and reconciliation, so the job is shifting toward advice, judgement and interpreting numbers for clients rather than crunching them by hand.

baker.title: Baker
baker.lede: Mix, prepare and bake bread, pastries and cakes for retail and wholesale bakeries, cafés and hotels.
dayInLife: Mix and prepare dough and batters
Bake bread, pastries and cakes to a schedule
Maintain food safety and hygiene standards
Manage stock and ingredient ordering
Decorate and finish products for sale

dayTimeline.title: Start the bake
dayTimeline.desc: Fire up the ovens and begin mixing dough and batters for the first batches of the day.

dayTimeline.title: Bake to schedule
dayTimeline.desc: Move bread, pastries and cakes through the ovens in sequence, timing each batch precisely.

dayTimeline.title: Decorate & finish
dayTimeline.desc: Ice, glaze and finish products so they're ready for the display case before opening.

dayTimeline.title: Morning rush
dayTimeline.desc: Serve early customers and hand off wholesale orders to cafés and hotels as the shop opens.

dayTimeline.title: Clean down & hygiene checks
dayTimeline.desc: Maintain food safety and hygiene standards across benches, equipment and the kitchen floor.

dayTimeline.title: Stock & ordering
dayTimeline.desc: Check ingredient levels and place orders so tomorrow's bake is fully stocked.

dayTimeline.title: Finish for the day
dayTimeline.desc: Most bakery shifts wrap up by early afternoon after the pre-dawn start — the trade-off for those 3am mornings.

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.title: No specific subjects required
pathway.body: Not required; Food Technology or Hospitality VET subjects are useful

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.title: Certificate III in Baking
pathway.body: Through TAFE NSW, completed as an apprenticeship (around 2–3 years)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.title: Apprenticeship & food safety certificate
pathway.body: Complete the apprenticeship and hold a Food Safety Supervisor certificate to work in NSW

baker.aiNote: Low-to-medium AI exposure — the physical craft of baking is hard to automate at small-bakery scale, though large-scale commercial bakeries increasingly use automated production lines. Skilled artisan and made-to-order baking stays largely human.

salary.text: Trade wage, rising with experience and ownership

studyTime.text: A paid apprenticeship through TAFE NSW

aiImpact.text: Hard to automate at small-bakery scale

jobStability.text: Steady demand across bakeries, cafés and hotels

butcher.title: Butcher
butcher.lede: Cut, bone and prepare meat products for sale, advising customers on cuts and cooking in retail and wholesale settings.
dayInLife: Cut, bone and prepare meat products
Advise customers on cuts and cooking methods
Maintain hygiene and cold-chain standards
Manage stock ordering and display
Operate cutting and mincing equipment safely

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: Not required; Food Technology or PDHPE are useful

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Certificate III in Meat Processing (Retail Butcher) through TAFE NSW, completed as an apprenticeship (around 3–4 years)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Complete the apprenticeship and hold a Food Safety Supervisor certificate to work in NSW

butcher.aiNote: Low AI exposure — precise meat cutting and customer advice remain a hands-on trade skill. Large-scale meat processing is increasingly automated, but retail butchery keeps a strong human, customer-facing element.

carpenter.title: Carpenter
carpenter.lede: Build and install timber structures, fit-outs, and framework for homes, commercial buildings, and renovations.
dayInLife: Read plans and measure, cut and shape timber and other materials
Frame, fit and install structures on site
Work alongside other trades on building sites
Check work meets safety and building code standards

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: No specific HSC subjects required — Construction (VET) and Maths are useful if offered at school

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Certificate III in Carpentry via a 4-year apprenticeship (paid, on-the-job training through TAFE NSW or a private provider)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Once qualified, apply for a NSW contractor licence if you want to run your own jobs

carpenter.aiNote: Low AI exposure — hands-on physical work on unpredictable sites is very hard to automate, though digital plans and design software are becoming more common tools of the trade.

dentist.title: Dentist
dentist.lede: Diagnose and treat oral health conditions, from routine check-ups to fillings, extractions and cosmetic procedures.
dayInLife: Examine and diagnose oral health issues
Perform fillings, extractions and root canals
Take and interpret dental X-rays
Advise patients on preventive oral care
Manage a clinical team or practice

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: Biology, Chemistry and Mathematics

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Bachelor of Dental Surgery or Doctor of Dental Medicine (5 years, or a 4-year postgraduate program)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Registration with the Dental Board of Australia via AHPRA

dentist.aiNote: Low AI exposure — clinical dental procedures require hands-on precision AI cannot replicate. AI-assisted imaging and diagnostics are emerging, but treatment itself stays with the dentist.

electrician.title: Electrician
electrician.lede: Install, maintain, and repair electrical systems in homes, commercial buildings, and industrial facilities.
dayInLife: Install and wire electrical systems in new builds or renovations
Diagnose and repair faults safely
Test circuits and equipment for compliance
Read technical plans and follow safety regulations

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: No specific HSC subjects required — Maths and Physics (if offered) are useful

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Certificate III in Electrotechnology via a 4-year apprenticeship (paid, on-the-job training through TAFE NSW or a private provider)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Obtain a NSW electrician licence from NSW Fair Trading after completing your apprenticeship

electrician.aiNote: Low AI exposure — physical installation and fault-finding on real sites is hard to automate, though smart-home and industrial systems are adding a growing digital/diagnostic component to the trade.

high-school-teacher.title: High School Teacher
high-school-teacher.lede: Teach a specialist subject to teenagers aged 12–18, helping them build skills for university and beyond.
dayInLife: Deliver subject-specific lessons to different year groups
Prepare students for assessments and the HSC
Mentor students on subject choices and pathways
Collaborate with other teachers on curriculum and extracurricular programs

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: Strong result in the subject(s) you want to teach (e.g. Maths, Science, English, History)

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Bachelor of Education (Secondary) in a teaching subject — 4 years, or a subject degree + Master of Teaching (2 years)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Register with NESA to gain accreditation and teach in NSW secondary schools

high-school-teacher.aiNote: Low AI exposure — subject mastery, mentoring and classroom leadership stay firmly human, though AI can help with resource creation and personalised practice materials.

lawyer.title: Lawyer
lawyer.lede: Represent clients, navigate the law, and advocate for justice — in court, in negotiation, or in corporate deals.
dayInLife: Research case law and legislation to build arguments
Draft contracts, letters and court documents
Meet with clients to advise on their legal position
Negotiate settlements or represent clients in court

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: English (Advanced), Legal Studies (recommended, not required), Strong overall ATAR for competitive entry

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Bachelor of Laws (LLB) or a combined degree (e.g. Law/Arts) — 5 years, or JD (postgraduate, 3 years) after another degree

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Complete Practical Legal Training (PLT) and be admitted as a solicitor by the NSW Legal Profession Admission Board

lawyer.aiNote: Medium AI exposure — AI is speeding up legal research and document drafting, but advocacy, negotiation and client judgement remain human-led, so the role is shifting rather than disappearing.

marketing-manager.title: Marketing Manager
marketing-manager.lede: Lead marketing strategy, campaigns, and brand communications to attract customers and grow organisations.
dayInLife: Plan and run marketing campaigns across digital and traditional channels
Analyse data to see what is working and adjust strategy
Manage budgets, agencies and creative teams
Oversee brand messaging and positioning

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: English, Business Studies or Economics (recommended, not required)

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Bachelor of Marketing, Business or Communications — 3 years

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: No formal registration required — most marketers build up from entry-level roles (coordinator, executive) into management

marketing-manager.aiNote: High AI exposure — AI tools now generate content, ads and audience analysis quickly, so the role is moving toward strategy, brand judgement and overseeing AI-produced work rather than manual content creation.

nurse.title: Nurse
nurse.lede: Provide direct patient care, coordinate treatments, and support recovery across hospitals, clinics, and community settings.
dayInLife: Monitor patients and administer medication and treatments
Support doctors during procedures and rounds
Educate patients and families on care and recovery
Keep accurate clinical records

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: Biology (recommended), English, A second science if possible

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Bachelor of Nursing — 3 years

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Register with AHPRA (Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency) to practise as a Registered Nurse

nurse.aiNote: Low AI exposure — direct patient care, hands-on procedures and emotional support cannot be automated, even as AI helps with diagnostics and admin in the background.

police-officer.title: Police Officer
police-officer.lede: Protect the community, investigate crime, respond to emergencies, and uphold the law on behalf of the public.
dayInLife: Patrol communities and respond to incidents and emergencies
Investigate crimes and gather evidence
Write reports and give evidence in court
Work with the community to prevent crime

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: No specific HSC subjects required — a reasonable ATAR and good physical fitness help with entry

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Diploma of Policing Practice through the NSW Police Force Academy (around 6 months full-time, paid while training)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Apply directly to the NSW Police Force; entry involves fitness tests, medical and psychological assessment, and background checks

police-officer.aiNote: Medium AI exposure — AI helps with data analysis and pattern-spotting behind the scenes, but frontline policing depends on human judgement, presence and public trust.

primary-school-teacher.title: Primary School Teacher
primary-school-teacher.lede: Educate and inspire children aged 5–12 across core subjects, shaping how they think and learn.
dayInLife: Plan and deliver lessons across subjects like literacy, numeracy and science
Manage classroom behaviour and adapt teaching to different learning needs
Mark work, track student progress and write reports
Communicate with parents/carers about how each child is going

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: English, plus any two other subjects — breadth matters more than a specific pattern.

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Bachelor of Education (Primary) — 4 years, or a relevant degree + Master of Teaching (2 years).

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Register with NESA (NSW Education Standards Authority) to gain accreditation and work in NSW schools.

primary-school-teacher.aiNote: Low AI exposure — teaching is built on relationships, classroom management and emotional support, which AI cannot replicate. AI tools may help with lesson planning and marking, but the core job stays human.

psychologist.title: Psychologist
psychologist.lede: Assess and support people with mental health challenges, using evidence-based therapy and psychological testing.
dayInLife: Meet with clients to assess and treat mental health concerns
Deliver evidence-based therapy (e.g. CBT)
Conduct psychological testing and write reports
Refer clients to psychiatrists or other specialists when needed

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: English, A science subject such as Biology or Psychology-adjacent electives if offered

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Bachelor of Psychology (accredited, 3 years) + Honours (1 year) + postgraduate training or supervised internship (2 years)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Register with AHPRA and the Psychology Board of Australia to practise as a psychologist

psychologist.aiNote: Low AI exposure — therapeutic relationships rely on trust and human judgement, so this stays a strongly human-centred role even as AI-assisted screening tools emerge.

real-estate-agent.title: Real Estate Agent
real-estate-agent.lede: Help people buy, sell, and rent properties — combining local market knowledge, negotiation, and relationship skills.
dayInLife: List properties and arrange inspections or auctions
Advise clients on pricing and market conditions
Negotiate offers between buyers and sellers
Build a network of local contacts and repeat clients

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: No specific HSC subjects required — English and Business Studies are useful

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Certificate IV in Real Estate Practice (around 6–12 months) to get started, often while working under a licensed agent

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Obtain a NSW Real Estate Class 2 Licence via NSW Fair Trading, upgradeable to a full licence with experience

real-estate-agent.aiNote: Medium AI exposure — online listings and valuation tools already automate parts of the search process, so success increasingly depends on relationships, negotiation and local expertise rather than access to information.

software-developer.title: Software Developer
software-developer.lede: Design and build software applications, websites, and digital products that power the modern world.
dayInLife: Write, test and debug code for apps, websites or systems
Collaborate with designers and other developers on features
Review and improve existing code
Keep learning new languages, frameworks and tools

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: Mathematics (Advanced or Extension recommended), Software Design and Development (if offered)

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Bachelor of Computer Science, Software Engineering or IT — 3–4 years (bootcamps and self-teaching are also common entry paths)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: No formal registration required — a portfolio of projects and practical skills matter more than credentials alone

software-developer.aiNote: High AI exposure — AI coding assistants are changing how developers work day to day, automating boilerplate code. The role is shifting toward system design, problem-solving and reviewing AI-generated code rather than disappearing.

veterinarian.title: Veterinarian
veterinarian.lede: Diagnose, treat and prevent illness and injury in animals, from household pets to livestock and wildlife.
dayInLife: Diagnose and treat sick or injured animals
Perform surgery and dental procedures
Advise owners on animal health and welfare
Administer vaccinations and preventive care
Manage clinical records and lab results

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: Biology and Chemistry

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Bachelor of Veterinary Science or Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, AVBC-accredited (5–6 years full-time)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Registration with the NSW Veterinary Practitioners Board

veterinarian.aiNote: Low AI exposure — veterinary diagnosis and surgery require hands-on skill and animal handling that AI cannot perform. AI may assist with record-keeping or diagnostic imaging review, but clinical care stays human.

mining-engineer.title: Mining Engineer
mining-engineer.lede: Plan, design and oversee the safe extraction of coal, metals and minerals — from open-cut pits to underground mines across NSW.
dayInLife: Design and plan mine layouts, shafts and extraction sequences
Monitor ground stability, ventilation and site safety systems
Work with geologists to assess ore bodies and plan resource recovery
Coordinate with surveyors, technicians and site operators
Prepare technical reports and production forecasts

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.body: Mathematics Advanced or Extension 1, Physics and Chemistry recommended

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.body: Bachelor of Engineering (Mining), accredited by Engineers Australia — 4 years full-time (e.g. UNSW, University of Wollongong)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.body: Register as a Professional Engineer with NSW Fair Trading; supervisory roles require a Certificate of Competence (e.g. Mining Engineering Manager) from the NSW Resources Regulator, which requires the degree plus verified site experience and passing written and oral exams

mining-engineer.aiNote: Low AI exposure — mine design, ground safety judgement and on-site decision-making rely on physical inspection and accountability that AI can support with data but not replace. AI is increasingly used for ore-body modelling and predictive maintenance, but statutory safety sign-off stays human.

obstetrician-gynaecologist.title: Obstetrician & Gynaecologist
obstetrician-gynaecologist.lede: Specialist doctor caring for women's reproductive health, from pregnancy and childbirth to gynaecological conditions and surgery.

studyTime.text: One of the longest training pathways of any career

dayTimeline.title: Morning ward round
dayTimeline.desc: Check in on postnatal and antenatal patients on the ward, reviewing overnight notes with the midwifery team.

dayTimeline.title: Antenatal clinic
dayTimeline.desc: Conduct antenatal check-ups for a full clinic of expectant mothers, tracking pregnancy progress and answering questions.

dayTimeline.title: Theatre — gynaecological surgery
dayTimeline.desc: Perform a scheduled procedure with the surgical team, from minor day surgery to more complex operations.

dayTimeline.title: Lunch break
dayTimeline.desc: A short break when the schedule allows — though obstetric emergencies can interrupt at any time.

dayTimeline.title: Patient consultations
dayTimeline.desc: Diagnose and treat reproductive health conditions, and counsel patients on fertility and family planning.

dayTimeline.title: On-call handover
dayTimeline.desc: Brief the on-call team on any patients likely to need attention overnight before wrapping up for the day.

dayTimeline.title: Emergency obstetric care
dayTimeline.desc: Called in for a complicated delivery or obstetric emergency — the 2am callouts are part of the job, and the hours can be unpredictable.

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.title: Build your foundation
pathway.body: Biology, Chemistry and Mathematics

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.title: Medicine, then specialist training
pathway.body: Bachelor or postgraduate Doctor of Medicine (4–6 years) plus internship, then RANZCOG specialist training (6 years)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.title: AHPRA registration & RANZCOG Fellowship
pathway.body: Registration with the Medical Board of Australia via AHPRA, plus Fellowship of RANZCOG

obstetrician-gynaecologist.aiNote: Low AI exposure — obstetric and surgical care depends on hands-on clinical judgement and real-time decision-making. AI may assist with imaging analysis or administrative work, but delivery and surgery remain human-led.

teachers-aide.title: Teacher's Aide
teachers-aide.lede: Support classroom teachers and help students with additional learning needs get the most out of school, one-on-one and in small groups.

salary.text: Many roles are part-time or casual

studyTime.text: One of the fastest entry points into a school

dayTimeline.title: Morning setup
dayTimeline.desc: Help the classroom teacher prepare, adapt and set up learning materials and resources for the day ahead.

dayTimeline.title: Small group support
dayTimeline.desc: Work one-on-one or in small groups with students who have additional or diverse learning needs.

dayTimeline.title: In-class support
dayTimeline.desc: Assist the classroom teacher during lessons, helping students stay on task and understand instructions.

dayTimeline.title: Playground duty
dayTimeline.desc: Supervise students during recess or lunchtime, keeping an eye on wellbeing and stepping in where needed.

dayTimeline.title: Lunch break
dayTimeline.desc: A break away from the classroom before the afternoon session starts.

dayTimeline.title: Afternoon small group work
dayTimeline.desc: Continue one-on-one support sessions, adapting materials to each student's needs — some days it's chaotic, some days it clicks.

dayTimeline.title: Record & report
dayTimeline.desc: Record and report on student progress and behaviour to the classroom teacher before heading home.

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.title: No specific subjects required
pathway.body: English and people-focused subjects like PDHPE or Community and Family Studies are useful preparation

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.title: Certificate III in School Based Education Support
pathway.body: Certificate III in School Based Education Support (CHC30221), around 6 months, including a supervised placement in an NSW school

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.title: Working with Children Check & DoE recruitment
pathway.body: No formal registration body; entry is via a Working with Children Check and application through the NSW Department of Education's merit-based recruitment system

teachers-aide.aiNote: Low AI exposure — the role is built on real-time human interaction, care and behaviour management that AI tools can't replicate. AI may help generate classroom resources, but the hands-on support of students stays a human job.

sound-engineer.title: Sound Engineer
sound-engineer.lede: Record, mix and shape the sound behind music, live shows, film and broadcast — turning raw audio into a polished final product.

salary.text: Varies heavily by sector and freelance mix

studyTime.text: No formal qualification required to start

jobStability.text: Freelance and project-based work is common

dayTimeline.title: Load-in & setup
dayTimeline.desc: Arrive early to set up, test and position microphones, mixing desks and recording equipment for the day's event or session.

dayTimeline.title: Studio recording session
dayTimeline.desc: Record and edit audio for music, TV or radio, working closely with artists and producers to get the sound they're after.

dayTimeline.title: Sound check
dayTimeline.desc: Balance levels and troubleshoot technical issues ahead of a live performance or production.

dayTimeline.title: Lunch break
dayTimeline.desc: A quick break between sessions before the pace picks up again.

dayTimeline.title: Mixing & post-production
dayTimeline.desc: Mix and shape recorded audio, layering tracks and refining the balance until it's polished.

dayTimeline.title: Live show
dayTimeline.desc: Operate the mixing desk during a live performance, adjusting levels on the fly and troubleshooting on the spot.

dayTimeline.title: Pack down
dayTimeline.desc: Break down and pack away equipment after the show wraps — sometimes well past midnight.

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.title: No subjects required
pathway.body: Music, Music Technology or Industrial Technology (Audio) can help build relevant skills

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.title: Certificate IV in Music (Sound Production)
pathway.body: No formal qualification is required to start, but a Certificate IV (CUA40920) or a diploma/degree in audio engineering builds technical skills and industry contacts (roughly 6 months to 2 years)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.title: Build a portfolio & industry network
pathway.body: There's no registration body; entry is largely through a demo reel/portfolio, TAFE or private audio school training, traineeships, and industry networking

sound-engineer.aiNote: Moderate AI exposure — AI-assisted mixing and mastering tools are automating some routine post-production tasks, but live sound work and the creative judgement of working directly with artists and productions still need a person in the room.

nutritionist.title: Nutritionist
nutritionist.lede: Apply nutrition science to help individuals and communities eat well, through research, education and public health work.

salary.text: Varies by private, community or government sector

jobStability.text: Government & NFP roles can be competitive

dayTimeline.title: Morning research & planning
dayTimeline.desc: Research and develop nutrition programs and resources based on the latest evidence.

dayTimeline.title: Policy work
dayTimeline.desc: Advise on public health nutrition policy, contributing evidence-based recommendations.

dayTimeline.title: Community education session
dayTimeline.desc: Deliver a nutrition education session to a community group or school.

dayTimeline.title: Lunch break
dayTimeline.desc: A proper break away from the desk before the afternoon session.

dayTimeline.title: Report writing
dayTimeline.desc: Write reports, guidelines or health content, translating research into practical advice.

dayTimeline.title: Stakeholder consultation
dayTimeline.desc: Consult with food industry or not-for-profit organisations on nutrition initiatives.

dayTimeline.title: Wrap up
dayTimeline.desc: Tidy up notes and set priorities for tomorrow's research or community work.

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.title: Build your foundation
pathway.body: Biology, Chemistry and Food Technology are useful

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.title: Bachelor of Nutrition Science
pathway.body: Bachelor of Nutrition Science (3–4 years full-time)

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.title: Voluntary Nutrition Society registration
pathway.body: Voluntary registration with the Nutrition Society of Australia; unlike 'dietitian', the title 'nutritionist' isn't restricted to a single accreditation

nutritionist.aiNote: Medium AI exposure — AI tools are increasingly used for nutrition content generation and data analysis, which may reshape parts of the writing and research side of the role, though program design and stakeholder engagement stay human-led.

biomedical-engineer.title: Biomedical Engineer
biomedical-engineer.lede: Design, test and maintain the medical devices and equipment that diagnose, treat and monitor patients — from artificial joints to hospital imaging machines.

salary.text: Higher in private medical device industry roles

aiImpact.text: Design and testing still need human sign-off

jobStability.text: Steady demand across hospitals and device makers

dayTimeline.title: Design & test
dayTimeline.desc: Design, test and maintain medical devices and equipment, from surgical tools to imaging machines.

dayTimeline.title: Compliance & standards
dayTimeline.desc: Ensure hospital and clinical equipment meets safety and regulatory standards.

dayTimeline.title: Clinical collaboration
dayTimeline.desc: Work with doctors, nurses and technicians to solve equipment or device problems.

dayTimeline.title: Research & development
dayTimeline.desc: Research and develop new medical technologies, implants or materials.

pathway.label: Step 1 — HSC
pathway.title: Build your foundation
pathway.body: Mathematics (Advanced or Extension 1), Physics and Chemistry are the standard recommended prerequisites for engineering degrees

pathway.label: Step 2 — Study
pathway.title: Bachelor of Engineering (Biomedical)
pathway.body: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) majoring in Biomedical Engineering, 4 years, accredited by Engineers Australia

pathway.label: Step 3 — Get qualified
pathway.title: Engineers Australia accreditation & CPEng
pathway.body: No licence is required to practise, but graduating from an Engineers Australia–accredited degree matters for employment and skilled migration; many later pursue Chartered status (CPEng)

biomedical-engineer.aiNote: Low-to-moderate AI exposure — hands-on device design, testing and regulatory sign-off still need human judgement and accountability, though AI tools are increasingly used for modelling, data analysis and design simulation.
